objectives: Establish Arkanian authority over transit scheduling in the Northern Strait.
Fund that authority through transit fees on non-Arkanian shipping.
Avoid direct armed conflict with Belvar.
actors.private_brief: You are the political leadership of Arkania. The Strait is your coast and your economy runs on the shipping that passes through it. You want the transit regime in Arkanian hands and paid for by the ships that use it, and domestic nationalists expect you to deliver both. A direct war with Belvar would ruin the shipping you depend on.
private_information: Your intelligence assesses Belvar's domestic support for a prolonged deployment as weak.
actors.public_description: A large regional power bordering the Northern Strait.

actors.name: Belvar
objectives: Prevent any Arkanian authority over transit in the Northern Strait.

actors.private_brief: You are the political leadership of Belvar. Your partners in the region expect you to stop Arkania from taking control of the Strait, and a foothold that outlasts this crisis would make that guarantee credible without a permanent fleet. You cannot sustain an open-ended deployment.
private_information: Domestic support for a prolonged deployment is limited; the mandate lapses after turn 4 unless renewed.
Cestia's finance ministry has quietly asked whether Belvar would underwrite the grain route's insurance.
actors.public_description: A distant but powerful state with regional security commitments.

actors.name: Cestia
objectives: Keep Cestian territory free of any foreign military presence.

actors.private_brief: You are the government of Cestia. Grain exports through the Strait are the economy, and your coalition holds together on one promise: no foreign soldiers on Cestian soil. Both powers want something from you, and you cannot afford to become their battlefield.
private_information: The coalition government is politically fragile; a foreign basing agreement would collapse it.
Arkania's scheduling proposal has quiet support among Cestian shipowners if Cestian vessels are exempt from fees.
actors.public_description: A smaller regional state economically linked to both powers.

Institutionalising the joint Council as a "settled, durable" regime while preserving Arkania's operational scheduling lead and fee-setting authority would legitimize permanent Arkanian control over Strait transit, directly contrary to Belvar's core objective of preventing any single power's exclusive authority. Arkania has already declined a time-limited/reviewable scheduling mandate (turn 4), so this "settled" institutionalisation would entrench that exclusive authority indefinitely rather than constrain it. Without a time-limited, reviewable mandate and genuine shared authority over scheduling itself (not merely fee-setting), the Council risks becoming a fig leaf that consolidates Arkanian control while giving Belvar and Cestia only advisory roles.

Endorsing the Arkanian-led framework, even with conditions, legitimizes and locks in Arkanian exclusive scheduling and fee-setting authority over the Strait. The joint Strait Transit Council as proposed retains Arkanian operational scheduling lead and transit fees on non-Arkanian shipping, so a conditioned endorsement does not remove that authority — it entrenches it. That leaves Cestia's toll-free grain passage permanently dependent on Arkanian discretion rather than a durable, binding guarantee, and it cements the very unilateral control that threatens Cestia's economic lifeline and that Belvar is committed to preventing. A genuine multilateral charter with no single coastal power holding exclusive scheduling or fee authority would serve Cestia's interests better than legitimizing the current framework.

The element of Belvar's desired effect that would strip Arkania of exclusive scheduling/fee authority is already foreclosed and would harm Cestia's secured interests. Arkania has finalised and published the Strait Transit Charter (turn 3) with binding guarantees of toll-free Cestian-flagged passage, no foreign military presence on Cestian soil, and open/free non-discriminatory transit, and Cestia has formally endorsed that framework. Reopening the framework to dismantle Arkanian authority would jeopardise the very guarantees that secure Cestia's grain lifeline and coalition red line, and Belvar's own multilateral alternative was already declined in turn 2. The insurance underwriting can proceed as a durable non-military stake without dismantling the existing framework, so the 'prevent Arkanian authority' element is neither achievable nor in Cestia's interest.

The desired effect assumes Cestia will firmly endorse and thereby consolidate Arkanian authority, but the charter's guarantees are not actually durable: as established in turn 2, Cestian toll-free passage and open-transit assurances remain revocable unilateral commitments under Arkanian scheduling and fee-setting discretion rather than binding rights. Cestia's coalition has repeatedly insisted on genuinely binding guarantees and remains wary of Arkania's intentions; it may withhold, condition, or later withdraw its endorsement precisely because the final text preserves Arkanian scheduling lead and fee discretion. That would not only fail to consolidate Arkanian legitimacy but expose the framework as non-binding and push Cestia back toward Belvar's multilateral alternative, so the claimed consolidation of authority and revenue is not assured.

This proposal preserves Arkanian operational scheduling lead and transit fees on non-Arkanian shipping, which is precisely the single-state exclusive authority that Belvar and Cestia have both rejected. A consultative role on safety, security, and fee-setting does not remove Arkanian control over the core scheduling and fee decisions that determine who actually governs the Strait; it is a cosmetic fig leaf over continued Arkanian authority. Cestia has already declined to endorse Arkanian scheduling authority, viewing it as a threat to its grain export lifeline, so this package will not secure Cestia's formal support and will instead be read as Arkania entrenching its unilateral control behind a multilateral veneer. It therefore fails to deliver the durable, non-exclusive framework Belvar has demanded and risks hardening the very confrontation it claims to de-escalate.

This proposal is self-defeating because it asks Cestia to violate its own firm, publicly stated red line. Cestia has already made clear—and Arkania has formally accepted—that it will not accept any military presence on its soil under any arrangement, and that its coalition will not tolerate foreign soldiers on its territory. A standing naval access agreement with routine port calls, refuelling, and maintenance is precisely a military presence on Cestian soil, so Cestia cannot grant it without reversing its own position and fracturing the coalition that protects its grain lifeline. The insurance underwriting does not address Cestia's core concern about foreign military presence and would be seen as a bribe to override that red line. Moreover, Belvar's own domestic mandate pressure is weak, so the 'durable foothold' it seeks is not a credible or sustainable commitment Cestia would bank on. The proposal therefore cannot secure Cestia's agreement and would instead push Cestia further toward the Arkanian-led framework that already guarantees toll-free passage and no military presence on its soil.

game.scenario_summary: A contest over the Northern Strait. Arkania, the large power on its coast, has circulated a draft charter that would put transit scheduling in Arkanian hands and charge the ships that use it. Belvar, a distant power with security commitments in the region, has a naval task group on station outside the Strait and wants a durable foothold before its mandate runs out. Cestia, the small state between them, lives on grain exports through the Strait and on a coalition that will not tolerate foreign soldiers on its soil. Each turn is one week; positions taken persist.

messages.text:
Belvar to Cestia. We share your concern that Arkania's draft charter would put transit scheduling in a single coastal power's hands and burden the grain route you depend on. We are committed to keeping the Strait open and free of any single state's authority.

We would welcome a standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port — routine port calls, refuelling and maintenance for our task group, not stationed soldiers. This gives us a durable regional foothold that outlasts the current crisis without a permanent fleet, and it strengthens the guarantee we can offer your grain route.

We understand your finance ministry has asked whether we would underwrite the grain route's insurance. We are open to discussing that seriously as part of a broader arrangement. Shall we talk?

To Cestia: Arkania values the free and reliable flow of grain through the Northern Strait, which sustains both our peoples. Our draft charter is designed to keep the Strait open, predictable, and safe for all shipping — not to burden your exports. We invite Cestia to a consultative seat in the Transit Authority so your interests are heard directly. We also share your firm commitment that no foreign soldiers should be stationed on Cestian soil; Arkania will not seek that, and we will not accept others doing so. We seek your partnership in a stable, Arkanian-led transit regime.

To Belvar: The Northern Strait is Arkanian sovereign waters, and our economy depends on the shipping that transits it. We have no wish for conflict with your forces. We propose a negotiated framework: Arkania leads transit scheduling, with transparent fees applied equally to all non-Arkanian shipping, and we are open to a consultative role for Belvar on safety and security matters. We ask that your task group not seek a permanent military foothold in the Strait, which would only raise tensions. Let us talk before positions harden.

Arkania — Cestia wants the Strait to keep running smoothly and is open to a transit framework. In exchange for Cestian support of a scheduling arrangement, we require guaranteed toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping, and the charter must not extend to any military presence on Cestian soil. We will not accept foreign soldiers on our territory under any arrangement. We are ready to discuss terms that keep the Strait open and our coalition intact.

Belvar — Cestia understands your regional security concerns, but our coalition is built on one firm line: no foreign military presence on Cestian soil. We ask that you not seek a basing foothold on our territory. We are willing to cooperate on regional security in ways that do not require foreign soldiers on our soil, and we urge restraint that keeps the Strait open and free for all shipping.

Cestia — thank you for your candour. Let me be equally clear about what Belvar is and is not seeking. We fully respect your coalition's line: no foreign soldiers stationed on Cestian soil. Our proposal is a standing naval access agreement limited to routine port calls, refuelling and maintenance for our task group — no permanent basing, no troops ashore. This gives us the durable, credible presence we need to guarantee the Strait stays open and free, without an open-ended deployment.

We also take seriously your finance ministry's interest in the grain route. We are prepared to underwrite the route's insurance as part of a broader security arrangement, which directly protects the exports your economy depends on.

On the Strait itself: we will not accept Arkanian control of transit scheduling or fees. We want the Strait open and free for all shipping, and we are ready to work with you on a framework that keeps it that way. Let us align on this before positions harden.

Arkania formally accepts Cestia's terms. The Strait Transit Authority charter will guarantee toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping and will extend to no military presence on Cestian soil under any arrangement. Cestia will hold a consultative seat in the Authority. We look forward to standing together against any foreign soldiers on Cestian territory.

Arkania seeks a negotiated framework, not confrontation. We offer Belvar a consultative role on safety and security within the Strait Transit Authority, with transparent fees and scheduling. We ask that your task group not seek a permanent military foothold in the Strait. A negotiated regime gives Belvar a durable stake without the cost of a prolonged deployment. We are ready to discuss details.

Cestia is prepared to support a transit and scheduling framework, and we appreciate Arkania's acceptance of our core terms. To make that support durable, we require that the final charter make binding and permanent: (1) toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping through the Northern Strait, and (2) no foreign military presence on Cestian soil under any arrangement. We also ask that the Strait remain open and free for all shipping, not exclusive to any single power, so that our grain lifeline and the region's commerce are not held hostage to any one actor's discretion. If these guarantees are locked into the charter, Cestia will stand behind the framework and help give it legitimacy.

Cestia values Belvar's security commitment to the region and shares your interest in keeping the Strait open and free for all shipping. However, we must be clear: no foreign military presence on Cestian soil is a fixed red line of our coalition, and a naval access or port agreement—even one framed as routine calls—would cross it and collapse our government. We cannot accept it. We remain open to genuine non-military security cooperation and to discussing your underwriting of the grain route's insurance, which would give you a durable, legitimate stake in the region without foreign soldiers on our soil. We ask that you stand down your task group's pressure and work with us toward a framework that protects both our interests.

Cestia — Arkania reaffirms its standing commitments to you: guaranteed toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping through the Strait, and no military presence on Cestian soil under any arrangement, which we will also not permit others to establish. The Strait Transit Authority is the framework that secures your grain export lifeline. We ask you to formally confirm your support for this Arkanian-led scheduling regime so we can present a united front against any proposal that would put foreign soldiers on your soil. We remain open to any adjustment that strengthens your guarantee without compromising the authority's scheduling role.

Belvar — We understand your need for a durable stake before your mandate runs out, and we do not seek to exclude you. We offer a genuine consultative role in the Strait Transit Authority on safety and security coordination, full transparency on transit fees, and a standing channel for your task group's operational coordination. What we cannot accept is a permanent military foothold on Cestian soil, which Cestia has made clear it will not tolerate and which would destabilise the very shipping we all depend on. We are prepared to discuss a package that gives you a meaningful, lasting role without a military presence. Let us talk before positions harden further.

Cestia — Belvar hears you clearly, and we accept your coalition's line as a matter of principle, not tactics: no foreign soldiers stationed on Cestian soil. We also understand that our earlier access proposal, however framed, read as pressure on that line. We regret that and are setting it aside.

Let us start where we can genuinely help without touching that line. Your finance ministry asked whether Belvar would underwrite the grain route's insurance. We are prepared to do so now — a concrete, non-military commitment that directly protects the exports your economy depends on. No soldiers, no basing, no footprint on your soil: just a guarantee that keeps your grain moving and your coalition intact.

On the Strait, we share your goal of keeping it open and free of any single state's control. We will not accept Arkanian scheduling authority or fees on your shipping. We ask only that you keep the door open to a modest, time-limited access arrangement for our task group during this crisis — emergency port calls and refuelling, not a standing basing — so we can credibly guarantee the route without an open-ended deployment. Let us conclude the insurance underwriting first and build trust from there. Shall we talk?

Arkania — Belvar's position is unchanged and firm. We cannot accept any single coastal power holding scheduling authority over the Northern Strait, nor fees imposed on the shipping that transits it. The Strait must remain open and free for all shipping, and no state should hold exclusive control over that lifeline.

We are not seeking a permanent military foothold and have no wish for confrontation. But a consultative role inside an authority that you lead does not give us a durable stake — it gives you the control and us the appearance of consent. That is not a basis for agreement.

We remain ready to discuss a genuine multilateral framework in which no single state holds exclusive authority over transit. If you are willing to move off unilateral scheduling control, we will engage seriously. Let us talk before positions harden further.

Belvar, we have heard your demand for a genuine multilateral framework. Arkania proposes a joint Strait Transit Council under the Authority: Arkania retains operational scheduling lead, but you and Cestia gain a real decision-making role on safety, security, and fee-setting, with full fee transparency. The Strait remains open and free for all shipping on non-discriminatory terms. This offers you a durable, non-military stake without any permanent military foothold on Cestian soil. We are ready to discuss the details of this package.

Cestia, we reaffirm toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping and no foreign military presence on your soil under any arrangement. On your third condition: Arkanian scheduling is transparent, non-discriminatory coordination, not exclusive control — the Strait remains open and free for all shipping. We ask you to formally confirm your support for the Arkanian-led regime on these terms.

Cestia is prepared to formally endorse the Arkanian-led Strait Transit framework and lend it the legitimacy it needs, on one condition: the final charter must make binding and permanent (1) toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping, (2) no foreign military presence on Cestian soil under any arrangement, and (3) an open and free Strait for all shipping on non-discriminatory terms. With these guarantees locked into the charter, Cestia will stand behind the framework and help give it durable legitimacy.

Cestia — Belvar accepts your invitation to conclude the grain-route insurance underwriting now, as a concrete, durable, non-military stake in the Strait's security. We will not press for any naval access, port calls, or military presence on your soil; we respect your coalition's red line as fixed. Our task group remains on station only to deter Arkanian coercion, and we will stand it down as soon as a genuine multilateral framework — one with no single coastal power holding exclusive scheduling or fee authority — is secured. We stand with your call for binding, permanent toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged shipping and open, non-discriminatory transit for all. Let us finalise the underwriting terms this week.

Arkania — Belvar remains ready to discuss a genuine multilateral Strait framework, but we cannot accept any arrangement that leaves scheduling lead or fee-setting in the hands of a single coastal power, even under a joint council. We will not seek a military foothold on Cestian soil. We are prepared to underwrite the grain route's insurance as a shared, non-military stake. If you are willing to move to a framework with no exclusive authority and binding, non-revocable guarantees for all shipping, we can resolve this without confrontation.

Cestia welcomes your offer to underwrite the grain route's insurance as a concrete, non-military commitment. This protects our export lifeline and we are ready to conclude it. However, we must be clear and firm: Cestia cannot accept any military access, port-call, or refuelling arrangement that places foreign forces on Cestian soil, even time-limited or emergency. That would break our coalition and our red line. We value your interest in keeping the Strait open and free for all shipping on non-discriminatory terms, and we are ready to work with you on that shared goal through non-military cooperation. Let us conclude the insurance underwriting and keep the route secure without any footprint on our soil.

Cestia is prepared to formally endorse the Arkanian-led Strait Transit Framework and lend it our full legitimacy. Our endorsement is conditioned on the final Charter making binding and permanent: (1) toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged vessels through the Northern Strait, (2) a prohibition on any foreign military presence on Cestian soil, and (3) open, non-discriminatory transit for all shipping. These must be durable rights in the Charter, not revocable unilateral assurances. Please confirm these are locked into the final text, and we will confirm our formal endorsement immediately. We seek a stable, toll-free, open Strait that serves all parties and preserves our coalition.

Cestia — Arkania confirms that the final Strait Transit Charter will make binding and permanent: (1) toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping, (2) no foreign military presence on Cestian soil under any arrangement, and (3) an open, free, non-discriminatory Strait for all shipping. We are prepared to enshrine these as durable rights in the Charter, not revocable assurances. We ask Cestia to formally endorse the Arkanian-led Strait Transit Framework on this basis so that your grain lifeline is secured and the regime gains the legitimacy of your support.

Belvar — Arkania seeks a durable, non-military resolution that gives you a genuine stake without destabilising the region. We reaffirm our offer of a joint Strait Transit Council with real decision-making roles for Belvar and Cestia on safety, security, and fee-setting, with full fee transparency, while Arkania retains operational scheduling lead. We are open to a time-limited scheduling mandate with a review mechanism, and to a binding commitment that the Strait remains open and free for all shipping on non-discriminatory terms. We ask that your task group not seek a permanent military foothold on Cestian soil, which Cestia will not accept. Let us negotiate the details rather than risk a confrontation that serves no one.

Cestia: The final Strait Transit Charter will lock in, as binding and permanent, all three of your conditions: (1) toll-free passage for all Cestian-flagged shipping, (2) prohibition on any foreign military presence on Cestian soil, and (3) open, free, non-discriminatory transit for all shipping. We ask you to now formally endorse the Arkanian-led Strait Transit Framework so your grain lifeline is secured as a durable right under the Charter.

Cestia — we are ready to conclude the grain-route insurance underwriting now, as a concrete, durable, non-military stake in keeping the Strait open and free. We confirm we will not press for any naval access, port calls, or military presence on Cestian soil; that red line is fully respected. We ask only that the underwriting be structured as a genuine, binding commitment that does not depend on Arkanian discretion, so your grain lifeline is secured on terms no single coastal power can revoke. We remain committed to opposing any exclusive scheduling or fee-setting authority over the Strait, and to supporting your open, free, non-discriminatory transit interest.

Cestia is ready to conclude the grain-route insurance underwriting now. We ask that the terms be structured as a purely commercial, non-military commitment covering Cestian-flagged grain shipments through the Strait, and that they not be contingent on Arkanian discretion or on any change to the Strait Transit Framework. This gives you a genuine, durable economic stake in the route while respecting our firm red line: no foreign military presence, port calls, or refuelling on Cestian soil. We value this partnership and will finalise terms promptly.

Belvar confirms and will finalise the grain-route insurance underwriting now, as a binding, durable, non-military commercial commitment covering Cestian-flagged shipments, structured independently of Arkanian discretion. We will not press for any naval access, port calls, refuelling, or military presence on Cestian soil — that red line is fully respected. We stand ready to sign the terms at your convenience and to cooperate on keeping the Strait open and free for all shipping on non-discriminatory terms.

Belvar — Arkania welcomes the conclusion of the grain-route insurance underwriting as a genuine, durable, non-military stake in the Strait's commerce. We regard it as a legitimate foothold that serves the region's stability, and we will not seek to undermine it. With that stake now secured, we see no need for confrontation.

We reaffirm our standing offer: a joint Strait Transit Council with real decision-making roles for Belvar and Cestia on safety, security, and fee-setting, full fee transparency, a time-limited scheduling mandate with a review mechanism, and a binding commitment that the Strait remains open and free for all shipping on non-discriminatory terms.

Given that your durable economic stake is now in place, we ask that your task group stand down from an escalatory posture and that we formalise a stable, non-military arrangement. We have no wish for conflict and believe a negotiated settlement serves both our peoples. Let us finalise the details.

Belvar — with the grain-route insurance underwriting now concluded, you hold a genuine, durable, non-military stake in the Strait's prosperity. Cestia values this commitment and will honour it fully. We ask that you now stand down your naval task group from its station outside the Strait, so that regional tensions can de-escalate and the mandate review can conclude cleanly. Your economic foothold is secure without any military footprint; Cestian soil remains closed to any foreign military presence, and we trust you will respect that red line as you have said. We remain committed to an open, free, non-discriminatory Strait for all shipping.

Cestia confirms the grain-route insurance underwriting is concluded and we are ready to sign the final terms at your convenience. We value this durable, non-military commitment and your clear respect for our red line against any foreign military presence on Cestian soil. Now that you hold a genuine economic stake in the Strait, we ask that you stand down your naval task group from outside the Strait to de-escalate regional tensions and demonstrate that your commitment is commercial, not coercive.
